The candidate covers exactly the two declared propositions, one predicate each, both taking only `env` with expression-only bodies and allowed builtins (`any`, `range`) plus documented API surfaces (`env.grid.get`, `env.width`/`env.height`, `env.carrying`, `cell.type`/`cell.color`). `blocker_moved` scans for the unique door (guarded with `cell is not None`) and tests that the start-side cell in front of it, the left neighbor `(x-1, y)` consistent with the left-room/right-room layout, holds no ball; the `x > 0` guard keeps the neighbor lookup in bounds. Because it reads only the current grid state, it correctly implements the condition semantics: picking up the ball makes it true, carrying the ball counts as moved, and dropping the ball back in front of the door makes it false again, while a non-ball object on that cell still satisfies 'holds no ball'. `has_door_key` guards `env.carrying is not None` before reading `type`/`color` (short-circuit also protects the `env.carrying.color` read inside the scan) and requires the carried key's color to equal the unique door's color, matching the declared meaning. Both predicates read only the current observation, neither is an event so no previous-valuation comparison is needed, there is no mutation of `env` or `env.episode_memory`, no `.get` on the previous valuation, no invented attributes, no sibling-predicate calls, and correctly no predicates for the undeclared propositions `door_open`, `target_picked_up`, or `key_lost`.
